notes:
BLOCKED on HELPER_MISSING: the pinned repository is a Gazebo Sim plugin library, not a ROS node and not an importable Python device. The card's family:ros/RosDriver is a package-scan artifact: package.xml:11 declares ament_cmake, but CMakeLists.txt:5-9 makes ament optional ('if ROS is not available'), and the clone contains no ROS topic, service, action or client dependency (no rclcpp, rclpy, rospy, roscpp, std_msgs or sensor_msgs occurrence). README.md:7-22 describes 'the official ArduPilot plugin for Gazebo' that 'connects to ArduPilot SITL'. The build produces only shared plugin libraries: CMakeLists.txt:94-99, 107-110, 118-121 and 131-139. It has no add_executable or add_test and no Python file (0 .py files in git ls-tree HEAD).

The primary runtime interface is the binary SITL UDP protocol, not ROS: ArduPilotPlugin is a gz::sim::System (include/ArduPilotPlugin.hh:92-97) whose SocketUDP receives servo_packet_16/32 from SITL (include/ArduPilotPlugin.hh:34-47; include/SocketUDP.hh:38-61; src/ArduPilotPlugin.cc:230-239, 1285-1295, 1486-1520), applies the resulting joint forces in PreUpdate (src/ArduPilotPlugin.cc:1204-1229), and sends JSON state back to SITL (src/ArduPilotPlugin.cc:1715-1718, 2026-2035). The other exposed controls are Gazebo Transport topics, not ROS: the zoom command /model/<model>/sensor/<sensor>/zoom/cmd_zoom (src/CameraZoomPlugin.cc:370-378), the parachute command /model/<model>/parachute/cmd_release (src/ParachutePlugin.cc:226-249), and camera image/enable_streaming topics plus a GStreamer UDP H.264 pipeline (src/GstCameraPlugin.cc:203-232, 408-431; README.md:203-232).

RosDriver can bind only rosbridge ROS endpoints and requires a source-cited ROS name and ROS message/service/action type syntax (MHS/sdk/docs/ros-driver.md:5-9 and 27-43). Declaring these gz.msgs or GStreamer topics as ROS endpoints would invent the interface; G7's ROS checker requires package/msg|srv|action type syntax, which no gz type satisfies. A direct Driver is equally impossible: native must name a Python class in the clone, or use a pyfile: selector for a Python file in it (MHS/sdk/docs/driver-authoring.md:171-194, 277-279, 321 and 377), and the pinned tree has no Python module, so a native.py factory would be a fabricated native rather than a port. GymnasiumDriver and MujocoDriver do not apply: the repository has no Gymnasium environment, action space, reward or MuJoCo model; tests/ contains only four SDF worlds. The independent source preflight reached the same disposition: work/handoff-runs/mhs-build-20261102/development/ros-next-batch-preflight-v1/PREFLIGHT.md:709-712 states the plugin 'does not expose the ROS flight-control API of a different ArduPilot repository' and 'A non-ROS transport/helper task requires separate routing, not invented ROS endpoints.'

Recon summary (no driver authored): the native reads are the binary servo PWM packet from SITL over UDP and Gazebo sensor topics (include/ArduPilotPlugin.hh:34-47; src/ArduPilotPlugin.cc:1486-1520, 1165-1188); the writes are joint force/velocity command components applied in PreUpdate (src/ArduPilotPlugin.cc:1204-1229), the JSON state sent to SITL (src/ArduPilotPlugin.cc:2026-2035), and the Gazebo zoom/parachute command topics (src/CameraZoomPlugin.cc:370-378; src/ParachutePlugin.cc:226-249). There is no ROS read, write or action. The only stop-like paths are Gazebo's paused flag, which merely skips the update block (src/ArduPilotPlugin.cc:1201-1202), the SITL-disconnect branch that calls ResetPIDs (src/ArduPilotPlugin.cc:1537-1543), and the Gazebo ISystemReset callback that reinitializes joint command components (src/ArduPilotPlugin.cc:397-420); none is an acknowledged ROS stop service/action. Units and ranges are not stated by the plugin: the wire fields are raw uint16 magic/frame_rate/frame_count/pwm (include/ArduPilotPlugin.hh:35-47), and multiplier, offset and servo bounds are SDF-configured (src/ArduPilotPlugin.cc:128-142, 652-723); the 1.0, 1000 and 2000 defaults are constructor defaults, not sourced device limits, so no Limit is invented here.

The card has no entry_symbols and no models, so there is no entry symbol to verify; the blocker is the missing non-ROS transport/helper and the absence of any source-declared ROS endpoint. No gate run was made because no honest driver.py/fake.py can be built from this interface; a fake-only pass would require fabricating the ROS surface or a Python native. The clone was left unmodified, and no network, pip install, upstream execution or hardware was used. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: none in shape because no shape can be selected; the card's RosDriver helper cannot express this runtime and needs separate routing. NOT COVERED: all simulator and device behaviour, including the SITL UDP bridge, Gazebo Transport camera/zoom/parachute controls and any live or hardware deployment, because the package stops before implementation.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Confirmed the author's block: the pinned tree has no Python file and no ROS code (no rclcpp, rclpy, roscpp, rospy, std_msgs or sensor_msgs anywhere), ament is optional in CMakeLists.txt:5-10, and the build produces only the four Gazebo Sim plugin libraries (CMakeLists.txt:94, 107, 118, 131); ArduPilotPlugin is a gz::sim::System (include/ArduPilotPlugin.hh:92-97) that exchanges binary servo packets and JSON state with ArduPilot SITL over UDP, and its other controls are gz-transport topics, so the card's family ros is a package-scan artifact and no RosDriver, direct Driver or simulator-family package can be built without inventing an interface. The README says this plugin replaces khancyr/ardupilot_gazebo (README.md:7-9), whose card is already overridden to skip/sim-env, and vehicles are driven through ArduPilot SITL over MAVLink, the flagship gh.ardupilot/ardupilot card, so the reviewer proposes the same skip override. The reviewer changed no authored file; the gate run created check-report.json (G1, G2, G3 and G9 fail because there is no package; stable digest sha256:d3273ca3bbfaa9785fd834a0caabcad018acfb57297398bfc8d789a718976f27). For the human reviewer: No package code exists. The plugin applies SITL's servo commands as joint forces in Gazebo and also exposes gz-transport parachute-release and camera-zoom commands; an agent would drive the simulated vehicle through ArduPilot SITL's MAVLink endpoint, not through this repository.
